title: Impacts of Digital Health Interventions for Children with ADHD
author: ajamisam

steps.title: Process and Screen Studies
steps.instruction: Process collected studies using Microsoft Excel and Rayyan to remove duplicates and sort studies for inclusion or exclusion based on predefined criteria.

steps.title: Extract Study Data
steps.instruction: Manually extract specific data points and variables from included studies and program them into Microsoft Excel for synthesis.

substeps.instruction: Extract study characteristics: authors, year of publication, country, study design, sample size, study period, setting, and patient recruitment.
Extract patient characteristics: number of patients randomized into each arm, age, gender, status of condition, medication, and coexisting neurodevelopmental issues (e.g., autism spectrum disorder).
Extract intervention and control group details: intervention name, domain, administration route, and duration of administration.
Extract outcomes: outcome name, type (binary/continuous), measure, and time points.

steps.title: Verify Data Extraction
steps.instruction: Perform data extraction using two independent reviewers and resolve any discrepancies through consensus.

steps.title: Assess Quality and Risk of Bias
steps.instruction: Assess the quality and risk of bias of included studies using appropriate tools, specifically the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (v1) for RCTs (Higgins et al., 2011).

steps.title: Calculate Effect Sizes
steps.instruction: Determine effect size measures based on the outcome type, including a 95% confidence interval.

substeps.instruction: For continuous outcomes: Use Standardized Mean Difference (SMD) for data combination, including only data with a consistent direction of effect.
For binary outcomes: Use Risk Ratio (RR).

steps.title: Perform Statistical Synthesis
steps.instruction: Apply a random-effects model for the review to account for the high probability of heterogeneity in the included RCTs and other studies.

steps.title: Conduct Sub-group Analysis
steps.instruction: Pool and group studies for sub-group analysis based on specific factors and compare outcomes for interventions within the same domain.

substeps.instruction: Group by: Active controls (e.g., other active intervention) vs. no intervention in the control group.
Group by: ADHD on medication vs. ADHD not on medication.
Group by: Age (>12 years of age vs. 8-12 years of age).
Group by: Intervention domain, intervention setting, and study duration.
